With columns/rows bounded by the 32-bit signed header reads (<=2^31-1) and bits_per_pixel in {1,4,8,16,24,32} (lines 336-339), every conversion stride is <= the allocation stride: case 16 stride 2*(columns+columns%2) (line 756) equals 4*((16*columns+31)/32) (line 454) for both parities, case 24 uses the identical formula, case 32 gives 4*columns == 4*((32*columns+31)/32), and cases 1/4/8 consume <= bytes_per_line, so per-row pointer arithmetic stays inside rows*max(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL).

The ReadBlob result at 469 is consumed only after strict equality count==length (470): the failure set of a short read (count<length, including truncated files admitted by the length/8 sanity cap at 456) is excluded and throws InsufficientImageDataInFile, so a partially filled pixels buffer never reaches the conversion loops. The 16-bit conversion stride 2*(columns+columns%2) equals the allocation-time bytes_per_line 4*((16*columns+31)/32) for both parities of columns; verified for columns=2k and 2k+1.

evidence.reason: `dynamic` is declared at L331 with no initializer and is assigned only inside the L333-341 loop when `strcmp(name, ".dynamic")` succeeds; a file whose section list lacks `.dynamic` leaves it indeterminate (producer path fully shown). The statement indexes `shdr[dynamic]`, reading an Elf32_Shdr at offset `e_shoff + dynamic*40` beyond the only shown capacity, the `st.st_size` mmap at L23 (e.g., dynamic=1000, st.st_size=1000). No guard constrains the index; the missing fix is the initialization/status check (e.g., `int dynamic = -1;` with a `dynamic == -1` bail) or a check `shdr[dynamic].sh_offset + shdr[dynamic].sh_size <= st.st_size`. Primary CWE-125 OOB read; secondary CWE-457 uninitialized read.

`ehdr->e_shstrndx` is an Elf32_Half (0..65535) from the attacker-controlled file and, with `shdr` based at the unvalidated `&elf_map[ehdr->e_shoff]` (L176), indexes far outside the `st.st_size` mapping (worst case offset `e_shoff + 65535*40`, plus field size). No bound check on `e_shstrndx`, `e_shoff`, or `e_shoff + e_shnum*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr) <= st.st_size` exists anywhere in the fragment; the missing fix is exactly such a bound. CWE-125, decisively unguarded in both 32-bit (L178) and 64-bit (L824) copies.

In the DT_NEEDED case, `name = elf_map + shdr[dynstr].sh_offset + dyn[i].d_un.d_val` (L362) uses two unvalidated, file-derived values; `dyn[i].d_un.d_val` is an Elf32_Word (0..2^32-1) and `dynstr` itself is uninitialized when no `.dynstr` section matched (L330, assigned only at L336). The `%s` argument is dereferenced for reading by snprintf, so an out-of-mapping pointer yields an OOB read (CWE-125). No bound check on the offset or on `dynstr` before the read; the same pattern exists at L1008-1009.

`name = elf_map + shstrtab.sh_offset + shdr[i].sh_name` (L183) combines three attacker-controlled values with no shown test that the sum lies in [0, st.st_size); `strlen(name)` then reads until NUL, walking past the end of the `st.st_size` mapping (CWE-125). The L254 guard only checks the resulting string length and does not validate the pointer; the missing fix is a bounds check on `shstrtab.sh_offset + shdr[i].sh_name < st.st_size` before the read. The guarded `strcpy` at L255 is covered by this guard (write indices 9-14 are within the bytes strlen proved readable), so the write itself is not the failing sink.

The loop at L350 runs `i < count` where `count = shdr[dynamic].sh_size / sizeof(Elf32_Dyn)` (L346) derives from unvalidated `sh_size` (Elf32_Word) and an uninitialized/unguarded `dynamic`; `count` can equal 2^31/8 entries while the mapping at L23 is far smaller, so `dyn[i]` dereferences beyond the mapped region (CWE-125). No loop bound is tied to the shown capacity `st.st_size`; the missing fix is a count/size check (e.g., `shdr[dynamic].sh_offset + shdr[dynamic].sh_size <= st.st_size`). 64-bit mirror at L996-999.

64-bit duplicate of the deciding sink: `dynamic` (L977) is uninitialized unless a section named `.dynamic` matched in the L979-987 loop, and `sh_offset` is unvalidated; `shdr[dynamic]` reads an Elf64_Shdr at an attacker-influenced index beyond the `st.st_size` mapping (CWE-125, with CWE-457 uninitialized use). No initialization or status check is shown; the same witness applies as for L345.

assumptions: Capacity of the parsed image is `st.st_size` as passed to `mmap` at L23; all ELF header/section/program/dynamic fields are bytes of the attacker-supplied file.

ELFCLASS32/ELFCLASS64 branches are entered only through the shown `MODE == ELFCLASS32/64` equality (L30/L676); `e_shnum` is Elf32/64_Half (0..65535), `e_shoff`/`e_shstrndx`/`sh_size`/`sh_offset`/`d_un.d_val` are 32/64-bit words/halves with full unsigned domains.
`snprintf(value, 50, ...)` and `memset(value, 0, 50)` bound the `char value[50]` stack buffer, and `strcpy(flag, "   ")` exactly fits `char flag[4]`; these sinks resolve PRESENT.
limitations: Header-truncation over-reads (e.g., `ehdr->e_version` with a file smaller than the header, L36/L678) are not used as decisive evidence because reaching the branch depends on the unshown semantics of `get_elf_class`.
`flag2str_sh`/`flag2str` write into the 4-byte `flag` but their bodies are unshown, so those potential overflows are unconfirmable and demoted.

The `strcpy(&name[15 - 6], "[...]")` write at L255/L901 is protected by `strlen(name) > 15` (L254/L900), which proves bytes 0..15 readable so the write at indices 9-14 stays in-mapped; the dead write witness is excluded, while the adjacent `strlen` read remains an ABSENT sink.
64-bit cases mirror the 32-bit sinks; only the decisive 64-bit mirror (L991) is listed separately, the rest are covered by their 32-bit rows.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds write into triggeredTopics: the drain guard fires only when numTriggeredTopics == 64, so a call entering with value 63 can store twice (lines 29 and 53) and write index 64 beyond the 64-entry buffer; entry values above 64 also bypass the drain because equality is never re-hit.

evidence.reason: Deciding sink: the only capacity guard is line 3 'if (numTriggeredTopics == 64)', which admits entry value 63 (63 != 64, no drain). With a one-segment topic whose node has an untriggered terminatingWildcardChild, line 29 stores index 63 and increments to 64; the loop exits (stop == string::npos) and this store writes index 64, exceeding the 64-entry capacity implied by the guard constant and the line 2 comment. The guard is the mutated form of the required >= check (operator mutation) and fails IDENTITY/REACH/EXACTNESS: no check runs between the two increments. Primary CWE-787 out-of-bounds write.

Same absent protective statement: with entry numTriggeredTopics == 63 and a multi-segment topic, the second loop iteration reaches this store after the first increment (index 64 still admitted because the line 3 equality guard does not execute between iterations and admits N > 64 once overshoot occurs). Confirmed in-call growth (63 -> 64 -> 65) makes subsequent calls start above 64, permanently bypassing the == 64 drain. CWE-787 out-of-bounds write.

assumptions: triggeredTopics has capacity 64, derived from the shown guard constant 64 and the line 2 comment 'If we already have 64 triggered topics...'
drain() resets numTriggeredTopics (typically to 0); triggered flags on newly created Topic nodes are initially false so the line 28/52 guards admit the store.
limitations: topic.substr at line 10 is safe on all shown recursive-call paths (start = stop+1 <= size); the unshown top-level call's start/stop could only cause an uncaught std::out_of_range, not memory corruption, and is not confirmable here.
Wildcard-recursion stack depth (line 36) is not assessed; it is bounded by segment count in practice.
Storage class of triggeredTopics is unshown, so the generic CWE-787 (rather than CWE-121/122) is reported.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation carries a protective statement: the `local` dereference at line 31 is reached only after the `!find_site_by_name(...)` early-return guard (lines 26-29) excludes the NULL/not-found state, the PID-file write is bounded by `sizeof(cl.lockfile)-1` in snprintf (line 44), and all security-relevant status returns (`rv < 0` after read_config, read_authkey, check_config) are checked before use.

evidence.reason: Dereference of `local` guarded on its only path by `if (!find_site_by_name(cl.site, &local, 1)) { ... return -EINVAL; }` (lines 26-29), which admits only a found state in which the out-parameter assigned through `&local` is non-NULL per the helper's standard success contract and excludes the not-found/NULL state before the deref. Single-statement diff audit: the shown guard equals the correct protective form; dropping `!` or moving the check after line 31 would admit `local == NULL`, but that mutated form is not present. CWE-476 mechanism not confirmable because no NULL value is produced or admitted on any path to line 31.

Bounded write sink: the size argument `sizeof(cl.lockfile)-1` is the shown capacity of `cl.lockfile` reduced by one, so snprintf can never write past the buffer and always NUL-terminates; the format string is a literal, so `booth_conf->name` is passed as data, eliminating format-string injection. No OOB (CWE-787/122) or injection (CWE-134) condition is derivable from the shown arguments.

assumptions: Internal helpers return negative errno on failure and 0 on success, matching every shown `rv < 0` check (read_config line 5-6, read_authkey line 10-11, check_config line 36-37).
`find_site_by_name` assigns the out-parameter `*site` (here `local`) to a found, non-NULL entry whenever it returns nonzero (standard out-parameter contract; callee body not shown).
`cl.configfile`, `cl.site`, and `cl.lockfile` are character-array fields of the global options struct, so `[0]` indexing and `sizeof` are well-defined.
limitations: Callee bodies (`read_config`, `read_authkey`, `find_site_by_name`, `check_config`, `find_myself`) and the declarations/initialization of globals `booth_conf` and `local` are not shown, so no failure behavior beyond the shown status checks is attributable to them.
`booth_conf->authfile[0]` at line 9 has no shown NULL producer after the line 6 success check; the symmetric evidence bar therefore demotes any NULL-deref hypothesis there.
`sizeof(cl.lockfile)-1` is one byte conservative; the capacity-one-larger variant (`sizeof(cl.lockfile)`) would be equally safe, so that direction cannot be the pair's failure difference.
`find_myself`'s return (line 33) is intentionally discarded per the in-code comment and its result is not consumed by any shown security decision.

verdict.summary: Missing total-element validation for input_max: only input_max.dim_size(0) == depth is checked, so an input_max with a zero-sized dimension (e.g., shape (depth, 0), NumElements()==0) passes all guards and the per-channel loop reads input_max_data[i] past the flat buffer, an out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: The read input_max_data[i] is the sink: i ranges over [0, depth) from the loop at line 56 with depth = input_max.NumElements() (line 6), but the flat buffer backing input_max_data (acquired at line 31) has only input_max.NumElements() elements. The only guard on input_max is dim_size(0) == depth at line 12, which admits shapes with dim 0 == depth and any other dimension zero, e.g., (depth, 0), where NumElements() == 0 < depth. The constraint that would close this gap, OP_REQUIRES(ctx, input_max.NumElements() == depth, ...), is absent — the NumElements equality at line 16 checks input_min, not input_max. With input_max of shape (depth, 0), index i = 0 at line 66 accesses input_max_data[0] past the empty buffer (index >= NumElements), confirming CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: TensorFlow tensors may legally carry zero-sized dimensions (e.g., shape (depth, 0)), so NumElements() can be 0 while dim_size(0) == depth.
input.flat<float>().data() exposes a flat buffer whose capacity equals NumElements(); indexing beyond it is out of bounds.
depth >= 1 is enforced by input.NumElements() > 0 (line 20) together with input.dim_size(3) == depth (line 25), so the loop body executes.
limitations: A rank-0 input_max would make dim_size(0) itself fail with a framework CHECK error rather than cleanly reach the OOB read; the confirmed witness requires a rank >= 2 tensor with a zero trailing dimension.
Consequences are a read-only over-read (crash/information influence through the computed scale and output min/max), rated medium rather than high.

verdict.summary: Every failure set derivable from the shown fragment is fully constrained: `if (N > 0)` (line 35) excludes the N==0 divisor reaching `num_updates / N` (line 57), `StartsWith` (line 52) guarantees exact division/reshape, and the two `<= std::numeric_limits<Index>::max()` checks (lines 22, 29) prevent Index narrowing truncation. The parallel `params->dim_size(0) <= std::numeric_limits<Index>::max()` check at line 29 likewise keeps the functor's row-bound comparison in Index range.

TensorShapeUtils::StartsWith prefix equality on every leading dimension makes NumElements(updates) an exact multiple of N.
LookupResource returns a non-null Var on OK, so `v->tensor()` at line 4 is non-null on the shown success path.
limitations: The bodies of ScatterScalarFunctor/ScatterFunctor are unshown; their index-range enforcement and the exact production range of `bad_i` cannot be confirmed, so the functor-write sinks and the `indices_flat(bad_i)` reads (lines 47, 65) are not decisive in either direction.
`params->flat_outer_dims<T>()` (line 37) on a possibly rank-0 variable would depend on framework shape-inference invariants not visible in the fragment; no confirmed mechanism is shown.
A possible mismatch between updates inner dims and params.shape[1:] is not covered by the shown rank/prefix checks, but the resulting callee behavior is unshown and therefore not a confirmed finding.

The line-4 guard OP_REQUIRES(ctx, session_state != nullptr, ...) excludes exactly the failure value nullptr from every path reaching this line: same constrained variable, no intervening assignment or aliasing, executed on the only forward path, and the operator/boundary exactly cover the NULL-deref failure set. verdict.summary: A relative fileName whose first path component is ".." makes the line 5-7 predicate false, so the upload-path prefix is skipped and the value reaches saveTo() (line 25) and create_directories() (line 18) unmodified, allowing file writes outside the intended upload directory; no rejection of ".." components or canonical containment check is present.

(e.g., "../b"): has_parent_path is true and first component equals "..", so the inner conjunction is false, the whole predicate is false, and fsFileName reaches this sink unmodified and outside the upload path. The absent/mutated fix is a rejection of parent-directory components or a containment check before the write; the shown "!= .." clause only disables the prefix rather than rejecting the traversal. Every guard on the path admits the witness, so the write escapes the upload directory (CWE-22).

For an admitted parent-relative name such as "../a/b", fsFileName.parent_path() is "../a", which lies outside the upload directory; when the parent does not exist, line 13-14 passes and this call creates directories outside the intended root. The same missing ".." rejection/containment guard that protects saveTo also covers this sink, and its absence leaves the traversal confirmed (CWE-22).

assumptions: getUploadPath() represents the intended containment root, since it is the prefix applied at line 11.
saveTo(fsFileName) writes the file at the resolved path, per the purpose of HttpFileImpl::saveAs.
limitations: fileName has no shown call site, so an attacker-controlled channel is not established inside this fragment; the failure is demonstrated for any caller passing an admitted value.
The assert at line 3 is debug-only and does not constrain non-empty malicious names.
The secondary witness "a/../../b" relies on OS path normalization at open time; the primary witness "../b" does not.

verdict.summary: Compute dereferences the nullable accessors ctx->session_state() and ctx->tensor_store() with no NULL check before use; a sessionless kernel invocation reaches GetNewId()/AddTensor() with a NULL pointer, leaving CWE-476 reachable.

evidence.reason: Sink is the unguarded dereference of ctx->session_state(). The accessor's return value has no shown non-NULL invariant and no preceding guard constrains it (L2 is not a check; L5 and L8 execute after this line), so the failure set {NULL} is admitted on every path. The absent fix is a NULL check (OP_REQUIRES(ctx, ctx->session_state() != nullptr, ...)) before line 3; one-token mutation of that fix (dropping or moving it after the dereference) still admits NULL at ->GetNewId(), causing CWE-476.

Sink is the unguarded dereference of ctx->tensor_store() while evaluating the call target. No shown statement constrains the accessor to be non-NULL, and the OP_REQUIRES_OK status check applies only to AddTensor's return value after the pointer has already been dereferenced, so the failure set {NULL} reaches the call. The absent fix is the corresponding NULL check before line 5; CWE-476.

assumptions: OpKernelContext::session_state() and tensor_store() are standard accessors that can return NULL when the kernel runs without an attached session/tensor store; no non-NULL invariant is visible in the fragment, so NULL remains in the residual domain at L3 and L5.
TensorShape({}) at L8 allocates a single-element tensor, so scalar<ResourceHandle>() and flat<tstring>().setConstant at L15/L18 write only element 0 and are in bounds.
limitations: No in-fragment statement literally constructs the NULL; the S1/S2 finding rests on the accessors' standard nullable semantics plus the total absence of any shown guard or non-NULL invariant.
The handle dereferences at L15/L18 are excluded by the OP_REQUIRES_OK status check at L8 and were resolved PRESENT, not findings.

verdict.summary: The scalar check guarding input_requested_max validates input_requested_min instead, so an empty requested-max tensor passes and flat<float>()(0) performs an out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: input_requested_max is an entry-point tensor with residual domain of any element count (including 0) because the only guard on its path, line 31, tests input_requested_min.NumElements() == 1 instead of input_requested_max.NumElements() == 1 — the correct one-token form mutated by swapping the constrained variable for its sibling (SINGLE-STATEMENT DIFF AUDIT: ABSENT). No constraint on input_requested_max's shape appears anywhere in the fragment; line 16 constrains only input_max_vec to depth.

assumptions: input_requested_max is a caller-controlled op input whose shape is unconstrained by any shown code (entry-point provenance).
flat<float>()(0) indexes into the tensor's element buffer at index 0 of its NumElements()-sized array.
input_requested_min is constrained to exactly one element by line 24, so its own read at line 27 is in bounds.
limitations: If the runtime never admitted zero-element tensors for input_requested_max, the witness would be unreachable; no such invariant is derivable from the shown fragment.
A requested-max tensor with more than one element still reads element 0 in bounds; the flaw is specific to empty tensors.

The float division by requested_min_max (line 56) can divide by zero when both requested bounds are 0 on the QUINT8 path, but no memory-safety impact is derivable from the shown code, so it is demoted.

verdict.summary: PQconnectPoll dereferences the PQgetvalue() result in strncmp() without proving the result has a field or that the value is non-NULL: a server can reply to 'SHOW transaction_read_only'/'pg_is_in_recovery()' with a TUPLES_OK result having 1 tuple but 0 fields, or with a SQL NULL field, so PQgetvalue(res,0,0) returns NULL and strncmp() performs a NULL-pointer dereference.

evidence.reason: val is produced at line 1504 by PQgetvalue(res, 0, 0), which per standard libpq semantics returns NULL when field_num is out of range (res->nfields == 0) or when the field value is SQL NULL. The only shown guards (lines 1501-1502: res non-NULL, PGRES_TUPLES_OK, PQntuples(res) == 1) admit both states, and no shown statement adds PQnfields(res) == 1 or checks val != NULL before this dereference. The absent/mutated fix is the missing field-count/NULL guard; the surviving witness is val == NULL reaching the strncmp at line 1515, a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476).

Same pattern as line 1515: val is produced at line 1571 by PQgetvalue(res, 0, 0) under guards (lines 1568-1569) that check only res/resultStatus/ntuples, not PQnfields or val. A TUPLES_OK result with ntups == 1 and nfields == 0, or a SQL NULL field, makes PQgetvalue return NULL, which is dereferenced here by strncmp(val, "t", 1) — NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476), with the missing PQnfields/val guard as the absent fix.

assumptions: PQgetvalue() follows standard libpq semantics: it returns NULL for an out-of-range row/column and for a SQL NULL field value.

The server response is network-provided entry-point data; no invariant in the shown fragment guarantees the result of 'SHOW transaction_read_only' or 'pg_is_in_recovery()' has one column or a non-NULL value.
limitations: memcpy at lines 281-282 (conn->raddr.addr from addr_cur->ai_addrlen) is not assessed because the destination capacity is not derivable from the shown fragment.
strcmp(conn->last_sqlstate, ...) at 1129-1130 is not a finding because a NULL last_sqlstate is not producible from shown statements (producer pqGetErrorNotice3 body unshown).
Format-string uses are literal gettext strings with matched arguments and are therefore safe sinks; buffers/port/length checks at 132, 140, 174, and 1097-1104 resolve PRESENT.
Severity is low because the confirmed effect is a client-process crash (DoS) triggered by a malicious/broken server, not code execution or privilege escalation.

verdict.summary: The Eval dispatch validates only output->type (lines 15/17) before passing input1/input2 to EvalDiv/EvalQuantized; input tensor types are never constrained, so a tensor whose type differs from the kernel's output-derived element type (e.g., kTfLiteUInt8 input with kTfLiteFloat32 output) is admitted and the kernel reinterprets the input buffer as a differently-sized element type, causing type-confusion over-reads (CWE-843, CWE-125). The missing fix is an input-type equality/whitelist check before the dispatch.

evidence.snippet: EvalDiv<kernel_type>(context, node, params, data, input1, input2, output);
evidence.reason: Sink consumes input1/input2 whose declared types are unconstrained (only GetInputSafe index status is checked at lines 6-7/9-10). The only guard on the path, line 15, constrains output->type to float32/int32 but not the input variables; under standard TFLite kernel semantics the callee reads the input buffers as the element type implied by output->type, sized per the tensor shape. Witness admitted by line 15: input1->type == kTfLiteUInt8 with output->type == kTfLiteFloat32, so the uint8 buffer is read as float, over-reading whenever the byte size is not a multiple of 4. Absent fix: an input-type equality/whitelist check (e.g., input1->type == output->type && input2->type == output->type) before the dispatch; its missing form admits the mismatch (CWE-843 primary, CWE-125 secondary).

Same input-type gap on the quantized path: line 17 constrains only output->type == kTfLiteUInt8, and the TF_LITE_ENSURE_OK wrapper checks only the call's return status, not input1/input2 types. Witness admitted by line 17: input1->type == kTfLiteFloat32 with output->type == kTfLiteUInt8, so a float buffer is reinterpreted as uint8 elements (mis-sized reads inside the quantized kernel, CWE-843/CWE-125). Absent fix: input-type validation before dispatch.

assumptions: GetInputSafe/GetOutputSafe return non-NULL tensor pointers on success and NULL-on-failure is excluded by TF_LITE_ENSURE_OK (lines 6-13), so output/input NULL dereferences are guarded.

Standard TFLite typed-kernel semantics: kernels access input buffers via GetTensorData<T> where T derives from output->type, and index by the tensor shape; this makes an input/output type mismatch a mis-sized access.
Node-provided tensors are attacker-controlled via a model graph, so unvalidated tensor types are a reachable adversarial input.
limitations: Exact input buffer byte capacities are not shown in the fragment, so the concrete over-read arithmetic (element-size mismatch) follows the callees' standard TFLite semantics rather than a shown allocation.
The discarded return value of EvalDiv (line 16) is demoted: no failing production path is shown for the callee.
params/data raw-pointer casts (lines 2-3) are not dereferenced in the fragment and were not treated as sinks.

limitations: NULL data->backing flowing into the `%s` arguments at lines 24-25 and 36-39 is not confirmed: no shown statement produces or admits that NULL; it rests only on the unconstrained field domain, which is not a finding under provenance class (c).

Expected length depth/8*image->columns derives from attacker-controlled HDR.nRows (line 67/75) via image->columns (line 101) and depth from HDR.Type[1] (lines 123-149); witness count = expected-1; mutated fix: `if (count == -1)` instead of `if (count != (ssize_t) (depth/8*image->columns))`.

verdict.summary: Heap over-read in ImportQuantumPixels: BImgBuff is sized from ldblk = (4*MATLAB_HDR.SizeX) mod 2^32 (32-bit unsigned wrap), while the importer consumes columns*depth/8 bytes; the only guard (line 243) excludes zero but admits wrapped sizes such as SizeX=0x40000001 yielding a 32-byte buffer consumed as ~4.3e9 bytes.

evidence.reason: Sink: ImportQuantumPixels reads image->columns (=MATLAB_HDR.SizeX, line 236) pixels of depth/8 bytes each from BImgBuff, but BImgBuff's capacity is only 8*ldblk bytes, where ldblk = (4*MATLAB_HDR.SizeX) mod 2^32 (line 202, 32-bit unsigned wrap; SizeX is produced by the unsigned-int reader at line 25 with residual range [1,2^32-1] after the line 243 zero guard). Witness SizeX=0x40000001 (admitted by line 243, !=0; ReadBlob at line 295 reads the wrapped ldblk=4 bytes and passes) gives a 32-byte allocation at line 270 and a ~4.29e9-byte over-read here. The absent/mutated fix is a bound check on SizeX or an ldblk-vs-expected-scanline validation; the shown guards (243, 295) never constrain the wrap, so the over-read is CWE-125 with root cause CWE-190 at the ldblk computation.

Producer of the wrapped size: with 32-bit unsigned MATLAB_HDR.SizeX, 4*SizeX wraps mod 2^32 (e.g., SizeX=0x40000001 gives ldblk=4 instead of ~1.07e9), making the line 270 allocation (8*ldblk bytes) far smaller than the scanline the line 314 sink consumes; no check of SizeX against a maximum or of ldblk against columns*sample_size/8 is present.

BImgBuff capacity is (size_t)ldblk * sizeof(double) = 8*ldblk bytes per line 270.
limitations: The MATHeader struct declaration is not shown in the fragment, so the exact width of SizeX is inferred from the line 25 unsigned-int producer; if SizeX were 64-bit, the wrap would not occur for values in the 32-bit read range.

Reachability of the over-read requires SetImageExtent (line 265) to succeed for very large dimensions (resource- and configuration-dependent, e.g., disk-backed cache); the status check at line 266 correctly aborts on failure but does not protect the wrapped-size case.

The required bound statement is absent; the present guard mutates the fix into a size-truthiness check, so this sink resolves ABSENT and is the decisive over-read (CWE-125, heap).

Same unprotected buffer[pc] family: with patdata=1 and buffer[0]=0x81, the packed branch reads pb=buffer[0], increments pc to 1 (line 311), then line 315 reads buffer[1] past the capacity of 1 at line 289. No statement on the path from lines 288/297 to 315 constrains pc against patdata, confirming the second concrete over-read witness under CWE-125.

Capacity of the pattern buffer is the shown variable patdata (allocation at line 289), not a macro or external invariant.

The required fix — a `pc < patdata` (or `pc+5 <= patdata`) bound before each read — is absent, so the sink resolves ABSENT with CWE-125 heap over-read.

`nbu` (L5, `mp_ubyte[MP_MAXINSSAMPS]`) is copied verbatim from file bytes by `memcpy(nbu, insDataPtr, MP_MAXINSSAMPS)` (L112), so each `nbu[sc]` retains its full declared domain 0..255. The loop `for (sc = 0; sc < MP_MAXINSSAMPS; sc++)` (L228) then indexes `smpReloc` (L4, capacity `MP_MAXINSSAMPS`) with that byte; any `nbu[sc] >= MP_MAXINSSAMPS` (e.g. 255) reads out of the stack array at L229/L232. The required `nbu[sc] < MP_MAXINSSAMPS` bound check is absent (identical code at L597 in the 0x104 path), so the sink resolves ABSENT with CWE-125 stack over-read.

assumptions: MP_MAXINSSAMPS is the capacity of both `smpReloc` (L4) and `nbu` (L5) and is the loop bound at L228/L596; the value itself need not be known because any byte ≥ that capacity is out of range.
`phead[y].patdata`, `phead[y].rows`, and `header->channum` are attacker-controlled file fields read at L49, L264-265, L271-272.

`phead[y].rows*header->channum*6` (L278, L286) can overflow 32-bit arithmetic for file maxima; the wrap-to-small-allocation corruption path depends on unshown `new[]` semantics and is demoted.

verdict.summary: snprintf sizes are one byte larger than the shown ReserveString allocations (64 vs 63 at L24; tmplen+1 vs tmplen at L37), so a formatted output of length >= capacity writes its NUL one byte past the heap buffer before any post-write check runs; dec is only bounded below (L17), admitting dec >= 61.

evidence.reason: Decisive sink: tmpbuf is taken from `tmpstr = String(tmplen, ReserveString)` at line 35, whose shown allocation-size expression is tmplen bytes; snprintf with size `tmplen + 1` writes up to tmplen+1 bytes (tmplen chars + NUL), overflowing by exactly one byte. dec has residual range [0, INT_MAX] after the only shown constraint `if (dec < 0) dec = 0;` at line 17, so dec = 62 with d = 0.5 yields a 64-char formatted length, first tmplen = 64 (>= 64, line 33), and the branch is entered; no guard precedes the write (lines 38-39 run after it). The missing/mutated fix is the write bound `tmplen + 1`, which should be `tmplen` (or the allocation one element larger, `tmplen + 1`); the shown form is the one-too-large capacity variant. Mechanism: heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-122).

Second absent sink: tmpbuf is taken from `String tmpstr(63, ReserveString)` at line 22, whose shown allocation-size expression is 63 bytes; snprintf with size n = 64 writes up to 64 bytes, overflowing one byte past the buffer whenever the formatted length reaches 63 chars (e.g., dec = 61, d = 0.5 -> "0." plus 61 digits, length 63). The shown guards at lines 28-33 (tmplen < 0, tmplen < 64 / >= 64) evaluate only after the snprintf write, so the overflow byte is written before any realloc/size check; the correct protective form is n = 63 (or an allocation of 64). Mechanism: heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-122).

snprintf(tmpbuf, n, ...) writes at most n bytes (n-1 characters plus NUL), so a size argument larger than the shown capacity is an admitted over-write.
The %.*F output length for finite d >= 0 with precision dec is about 2 + dec characters, so dec >= 61 reaches a length of at least 63.
limitations: The comment at line 21 claims String(63, ReserveString) provides 63 characters plus a NUL byte; per the evidence rules, comments/documentation are not credited as protective capacity statements, so the code-visible capacity is the allocation argument (63 / tmplen).

No call site is shown, so attacker control beyond the declared parameter domains (d, dec, dec_point, thousand_sep) is not established; the finding is demonstrated wholly inside the fragment from the declared-domain values admitted by line 17.
Exotic multi-gigabyte dec_point/thousand_sep truncation paths (lines 67, 80 converting size_t back to int) were analyzed but not used as evidence, since no shown producer admits such lengths.

Per the evidence bar, an unshown capacity cannot be fabricated to declare an OOB, so this sink resolves neither PRESENT nor ABSENT and is demoted to limitations; it is not the deciding sink.

Sink: filesystem creation on a path whose residual content is caller-provided (no component bytes are copied into dst by this fragment). Failure set: any mkdir failure. Protective statement PRESENT verbatim: "!= 0 && errno != EEXIST" fully covers it; only EEXIST is admitted, which is a handled no-op that proceeds to the also-checked chmod. No status-handling flaw: errno is only read when mkdir returned non-zero.

Sink: chmod applied under the L17 gate (stat succeeded and S_ISDIR). Failure set: a failing chmod. Protective statement PRESENT verbatim: "!= 0" catches every failure and errExit aborts; s.st_mode is only read on the path where stat returned 0 (short-circuit &&), so no uninitialized use of s. Resolves PRESENT.

Sink: temporary terminator write into src. Failure set: index past the end of src. Protective loop-bound statement PRESENT at L9-10: "if (*p == '\0') { last = true; }" terminates the loop at the first NUL, so p is dereferenced only at indices <= strlen(src) and writes occur only at the NUL slot or at '/' positions strictly before it; the L28-31 "if (!last)" guard restores each slash. Resolves PRESENT.

assumptions: src and dst are NUL-terminated char arrays, as required by the fragment's own termination walk at L9-10 (the loop reads *p until '\0').

src_prefix_len/dst_prefix_len denote positions inside the strings immediately before a '/' + suffix (the algorithm's inherent precondition); violation of that precondition has no shown producer in the fragment.
limitations: OOB on *q='\0' (L20) and *r='/' (L21) is unconfirmable: the fragment never shows dst's size or allocation, so no index beyond capacity and no admitted witness can be demonstrated; demoted per the evidence bar.

Path traversal via '..' components is not confirmable in the fragment: the fragment writes only '\0' and '/' into dst and never copies component bytes from src, so attacker-derived component content reaching mkdir/chmod would require an unshown caller-supplied dst, which is out of scope.

A caller passing src_prefix_len >= strlen(src) would start p past the terminator (OOB read at L9), but that is an unshown precondition violation by an unseen call site, not a value admitted by any shown guard; demoted.

The chmod-after-EEXIST pattern could chmod an existing (in sandbox, not attacker-writable) directory; no privilege context or symlink-race witness is shown in the fragment, so it is a hardening concern only.

With count = ts_val - 1 - off <= -1, the unsigned expression at line 79-81 yields STRLEN(oldp) + s_len + count + 1 = STRLEN(oldp) + s_len, while the copies plus STRMOVE at 116 write STRLEN(oldp) + s_len + 1 bytes (allocation line 79-81 is the capacity reference); the missing fix is the removal of the count adjustment, so the heap write exceeds newp (CWE-787, downstream of the line-63 sink).

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in the fragment carries an exactly-covering protective statement: the ESIL backward scan is bounded by `addr >= esil_buf + 1` so no address below esil_buf is ever read; NULL results (r_strbuf_get/strdup/strstr) are checked before use; op->src[i]/reg/name are NULL-checked; frame offsets are capped to +/- maxstackframe (8192) before get_stack_var/r_anal_function_set_var; and all format strings are literal. evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the only unbounded pointer read (the backward scan from ptr_end through the strdup'ed esil_buf). Because *ptr_end is NULed at line 36, the scan actually walks backward, and the guard `addr >= esil_buf + 1` gives the invariant addr >= esil_buf at every condition evaluation, so addr[0]/addr[1] never dereference below esil_buf. The excluded set is every address < esil_buf; the boundary addr == esil_buf reads valid bytes (buffer >= 5 since strstr matched the >= 4-char pattern at line 31). A one-token mutation to `addr >= esil_buf` would admit a read of esil_buf[-1] (CWE-125); the shown +1 form is the correct fixed form and resolves the sink PRESENT.

assumptions: maxstackframe is the shown constant 1024*8 = 8192, so both `maxstackframe != 0` (line 90) and `maxstackframe > 0` (line 155) guards are active and bound frame_off to [-8192, 8192].
r_strf_var fills the 64-byte esilexpr with truncating snprintf semantics, so the pattern searched at line 31 is always NUL-terminated.
The strstr match at line 31 requires esil_buf to contain the full ',%s,%s,' pattern, so the strdup allocation is at least strlen(pattern)+1 >= 5 bytes.
limitations: get_stack_var/r_anal_function_set_var bodies are not shown; frame_off values admitted inside the +/-8192 cap are not shown to reach any memory operation, so no OOB can be attributed to them from this fragment.

strdup(r_type_func_args_name(...)) at line 122 is not a confirmed NULL deref because no shown statement produces NULL from r_type_func_args_name at an index where r_type_func_args_type already returned non-NULL.

Signed arithmetic in `ptr - fcn->stack` / `-(ptr + fcn->bp_off)` could wrap for extreme st64 values, but any wrapped frame_off outside +/-8192 is rejected by the shown caps and values inside the cap have no shown memory effect; no confirmed witness.

verdict.summary: atusb_disconnect dereferences the result of usb_get_intfdata(interface) with no NULL check; when the interface driver-data slot is unset or was cleared, atusb is NULL and the unconditional member write atusb->shutdown = 1 causes a NULL pointer dereference.

for (j = 0; j < nelements && i < sh.sh_properties;
			    j++, i++)

verdict.summary: In bgp_capability_msg_parse, the capability-length check at line 43 only verifies pnt + hdr->length + 3 <= end and imposes no minimum on hdr->length, so the fixed-size memcpy of sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) at line 51 can read beyond the packet buffer when an attacker sets a short capability length.

The only guard on the path, line 43 `(pnt + hdr->length + 3) > end`, admits hdr->length values as small as 0 and guarantees only that hdr->length bytes exist after pnt+3, not that a full struct does. With attacker-controlled hdr->length = 0 and end == pnt + 3 (a 3-byte capability header: action, code, length), every condition passes and memcpy reads beyond the valid region, an over-read (CWE-125). The absent/mutated fix is the missing lower-bound check `hdr->length < sizeof(struct capability_mp_data)` (or `pnt + 3 + sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) > end`).

assumptions: pnt points into the received packet buffer and length bounds it (end = pnt + length at line 13) — the only shown capacity for the packet region.
sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) is the fixed read size consumed at line 51.
limitations: The exact size of struct capability_mp_data is not shown; any size >= 1 makes the finding valid because hdr->length can be 0 and the remaining region can be smaller than any such size.
AFI/SAFI array indexing was not treated as a finding because bgp_map_afi_safi_iana2int failure is checked before the writes; its body is not shown.
The union/format-string call sites were not treated as findings because the format strings are literals and the arguments are scalar or host strings.

x0,y0,x1,y1,bbox,ptm and CTM values are PDF-attacker-controlled with full declared domains except xStep/yStep constrained to width/height at line 24.
Branch line 70-77 is reachable (e.g. width=height=xStep=yStep=0.5, ptm=0.5, HDPI=72 gives kx_old=ky_old=0.25 and normalized surface_width=surface_height=2).

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation in the fragment can be confirmed to reach an unprotected sink: the only paste sink (cmdline_paste at line 40) is gated by `if (c != ESC)` and no length/capacity argument is shown to make its failure set derivable at the call site; the cmdpos writes are fully constrained by the `new_cmdpos >= 0` check and the `new_cmdpos > ccline.cmdlen` clamp (lines 54-60); the only pointer dereference (`*gotesc`, line 47) has no NULL producer shown.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in the size computation (line 68, 32-bit arithmetic cast to long long only after wrapping) lets the line-69 guard pass with a small wrapped `allocate` while `count*size` remains huge, so io.read at line 79 copies up to 0xFFFFFFF8 bytes into a 12-byte heap buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow.

evidence.reason: count (uint32_t, file-derived, line 37) and size={1,2,4,8} (lines 58-63) have residual range count in [0,2^32-1]; line 68 computes `allocate = (long long) (size*count + pad+20)` with the arithmetic done in uint32_t, wrapping modulo 2^32 before the cast. Witness size=4, count=0x3FFFFFFE: size*count=0xFFFFFFF8, allocate wraps to 12; the line-69 guard (`allocate > (long long) io.size()`) admits 12 for any file >= 12 bytes (a 14-byte file already passes the line-14/34 reads), line 72 allocates DataBuf buf(12), and line 74 sets bOffsetIsPointer=true, so this io.read writes up to 0xFFFFFFF8 bytes into the 12-byte heap buffer - 13+ file bytes already write out of bounds. Same root cause as line 79: with the same witness (size=4, count=0x3FFFFFFE) allocate wraps to 12 and line 72 allocates a 12-byte buffer, but on the isPrintXMP(tag,option) path this statement writes a NUL at buf.pData_[0x3FFFFFFE], far beyond the 12-byte capacity - a CWE-122 heap over-write admitted because the line-69 guard only compares the wrapped allocate against io.size().

assumptions: size, count, and pad are uint32_t, so the line-68 expression `size*count + pad+20` is evaluated modulo 2^32 before the (long long) cast.

limitations: typeValid/isPrintXMP/isPrintICC callee bodies are unshown; they only gate secondary sinks, not the decisive line-79 read.

verdict.summary: The wrap-loop bookkeeping under-decrements len (len -= cut instead of cut+1), so the tracked length drifts above the true remainder and ptr advances past the 256-byte print_buffer. A long formatted warning (len >= 318 with spaces at each 80-char boundary) makes ISSPACE(ptr[cut]) at line 21 and fwrite at line 25 read up to 64+ bytes past the stack array (CWE-125), and for longer messages ptr keeps climbing while len stays positive, giving an unbounded over-read / crash.

evidence.reason: CWE-125 over-read of print_buffer (capacity 256 at line 7, valid indices 0..255). len is the unconstrained vsnprintf would-be length (line 11); the guards at lines 15 and 18 admit every len > WARN_TEXTWIDTH, and the mutated fix at line 28 (len -= cut) under-decrements by 1 per wrap vs. the 1..W chars consumed by ptr += cut+1 at line 27, so tracked len overstates the true remainder. For len = 318 with spaces at indices 79, 159 and 239, iterations 1-3 advance ptr to 240 in bounds, then iteration 4 still satisfies len = 81 > 80 and this statement reads ptr[79] at index 319, 64 bytes past the array; the correct protective statement is len -= cut+1.

Same root cause and witness as the line 21 sink: on the 4th wrap of a len=318 message (spaces at 79/159/239) the guard at line 18 admits len=81 > 80 and fwrite reads ptr[0..79] from base index 240, i.e., bytes 240-319, exceeding the shown 256-byte capacity. No protective statement on this path constrains ptr against the array size; the only candidate, len -= cut at line 28, is the off-by-one mutant of len -= cut+1.

PRESENT: the vsnprintf sink is exactly bounded by the shown capacity sizeof(print_buffer) = 256, so it cannot overwrite the buffer; its unbounded return value is what feeds the later, unguarded reads.

assumptions: print_buffer has the shown capacity of 256 bytes (line 7), giving valid indices 0..255.

WARN_TEXTWIDTH is a small positive wrap width; the witness uses the conventional value 80, and the claimed OOB also holds for larger widths (a width >= 257 makes even the first wrap read index >= 255, and any width with len > width eventually drifts past the array).

limitations: The duplicate va_start at lines 9-10 is undefined behavior but has no shown failing producer (it is a no-op on common ABIs), so it is demoted and is not the basis of the verdict.

evidence.reason: Deciding sink: 'count' originates from file bytes (L37, byteSwap4 of dir[4:7], full uint32 domain) with no shown bound. On tag 0x02bc with type tiffSShort (size=2, L59, admitted by typeValid at L41) and count=0x80000000, L66's 'size*count + pad+20' computes 0x100000000 in uint32, wrapping to 0+0+20=20, so DataBuf holds 20 bytes. L152 ('if ( isPrintXMP(tag,option) )') admits this count, and L153 writes at index 0x80000000 — heap out-of-bounds write. The protective statement (a bound/cap on count before the allocation) is absent; the only nearby check, the commented L65, is inactive. Primary CWE-787, with CWE-190 as the wrap root cause.

For a string type (size=1, pad=1) with count=0xFFFFFFFF, L66 allocates (2^32-1+1+20) mod 2^32 = 20 bytes while this read requests count*size = 2^32-1 bytes from bOffsetIsPointer (L68, count*size>4). No guard constrains 'count' between L37 and L73, so the requested length exceeds the shown capacity — heap over-write once io supplies the bytes. Absent fix: a count bound before the allocation/read.

For tag 0x8773 (isPrintICC) with an 8-byte type (size=8) and count=2^29, L66 wraps to (2^32+20) mod 2^32 = 20 bytes; this output read then consumes count=2^29 bytes from buf.pData_ — heap over-read admitted by the same unguarded uint32 overflow (L58-66). The absence of a count bound leaves the failure set admitted.

typeValid(type) (L41) admits TIFF types with size in {1,2,4,8} per L57-63; tiffSShort (size 2) and 8-byte types are admitted.
isPrintXMP/isPrintICC gate only on tag/option and admit any count value.

verdict.summary: Network-controlled hdr.nSubrects is multiplied by (4 + BPP/8) in 32-bit arithmetic at line 19; an overflowing value wraps the product small enough to pass the RFB_BUFFER_SIZE check, yet the loop at lines 24-30 then reads nSubrects*(4+BPP/8) true bytes from client->buffer, producing a heap over-read.

The one-statement fix (a division/bound check on mincount * l before line 1215, mirroring the check at 1031) is absent — line 1214 is blank. Sink resolves ABSENT; CWE-122 heap overflow, root CWE-190.

No protective bound check exists on this path — the fix statement is missing at line 1214. CWE-190 (secondary to CWE-122 at the copy sink).
